question.text:
Consider a language that allows identifiers to start with a digit if they contain at least one letter. How would this impact the design of the Lexical Analyzer?

  1. IT WOULD SIMPLIFY THE DFA BY MERGING CONSTANTS AND IDENTIFIERS
     
  2. IT WOULD HAVE NO IMPACT ON THE DFA STRUCTURE
     
  3. MIN DFA WILL REQUIRE $3$ STATES FOR THIS PURPOSE
     
  4. THE LEXICAL ANALYZER WOULD BE UNABLE TO PROCESS SUCH A LANGUAGE

$$
\begin{aligned}
& E \rightarrow T R \\
& R \rightarrow+T R \mid \epsilon \\
& T \rightarrow F Y \\
& Y \rightarrow * F Y \mid \epsilon \\
& F \rightarrow(E) \mid i d
\end{aligned}
$$


Which of the following statements regarding the FIRST and FOLLOW sets of this grammar is FALSE?

  1. $\left.\operatorname{FOLLOW}(T)=\left\{{ }^*,+,\right), \$\right\}$
     
  2. $\operatorname{FIRST}(R)=\{+$, epsilon $\}$
     
  3. $\operatorname{FOLLOW}(Y)=\{+),, \$\}$

question.text:
Consider the following grammar $G$ with non-terminals $\{S, A, B, C\}$ and terminals $\{a, b, c, d, g\}$ :

$$
\begin{aligned}
& S \rightarrow A B \\
& A \rightarrow a A \mid \epsilon \\
& B \rightarrow b B \mid C \\
& C \rightarrow c C \mid d \mid \epsilon
\end{aligned}
$$


What is the FOLLOW set of the non-terminal $A$ ?

  1. $\{a, b, c, d\}$
     
  2. $\{b, c, d, \$\}$
     
  3. $\{b, c, d\}$
     
  4. $\{B, b, c, d, \$\}$

question.text:
$\text { Consider the following C code segment: }$

inline int square(int s) { return s * s; }
void process(int n, int a[]) {
    int x = 10;
    int y = x; // Copy of x
    
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)
    {
        a[i] = y * i;
        int val = square(i);
        
        // Assume n is always a multiple of 4
        //
    }
}

Which of the following is/are not true?

  1. THERE IS SCOPE FOR COPY PROPAGATION IN THIS CODE
     
  2. THERE IS SCOPE FOR LOOP UNROLLING IN THIS CODE
     
  3. THE CODE EXHIBITS CONSTANT FOLDING AT RUNTIME
     
  4. THERE IS SCOPE FOR DEADCODE ELIMINATION IN THIS CODE
